newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Dole spar on taxes, economy in debate.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Dole spar on taxes, economy in debate.

text.p: President Bill Clinton blasted Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole's proposal to cut income taxes by 15 percent, or $550 billion, and warned it would drive up interest rates and slow down in the economy.

The two candidates sparred about taxes and the economy throughout their first 90-minute presidential debate, with Dole defending his tax cut plan and Clinton pushing his proposals for targeted tax cuts instead.

Clinton said Dole's tax cut proposal "will cause a big hole in the deficit, which will raise interest rates and slow down the economy and cause people to pay more for home mortgages, car payments, credit card payments, college loans and small business loans."

Clinton said Dole's proposal would actually raise taxes for nine million people, while forcing even bigger cuts in Medicare, Medicaid, education and environmental programs than those proposed by Republicans and vetoed by Clinton. A better plan, Clinton said, would be to pass targeted tax cuts for education, health care and home buyers.
Dole criticized Clinton's leadership on economic issues, saying that the economy was still expanding, but at a much slower rate than when Clinton first took office.
He said bankruptcies were up, wages were stagnant, and U.S. foreign debt was at its highest level in history.
The American people are "working harder and paying more taxes" than four years ago, Dole said.
Clinton defended his record, citing 10.5 million additional jobs, rising wages, record numbers of small businesses and the biggest drop in the number of people in poverty in 27 years.

At one point Dole got a laugh from the audience. Asked by debate moderator Jim Lehrer if he thought his tax cut was still a good idea, Dole said, "Oh yes, and you'll be eligible. And so will the former president."
To which Clinton smiled and replied, "I need it."
